newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds end week on sour note as rate cut hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Bunds end week on sour note as rate cut hopes fade.

text.p: Bund futures finished the week on a sour note as a several inflation reports and comments from the vice president of the Bundesbank quashed for the moment hopes of an interest rate cut.
The DTB March Bund future was down 25 basis points late in the day at 101.33, in the middle of the day's range of 101.17 to 101.34.

Traders said the inflation reports, for three German states as well as import prices, have robbed the ability of Bunds to show much upside potential next week and that they are now vulnerable to swings in the Treasury market.
Two west German states today ignited the inflation worries. Baden-Wuerttemberg said year-on-year CPI growth there was up 1.7 percent in January compared with a 1.2 percent yearly pace in December.
North Rhine-Westphalia, meanwhile showed yearly CPI growth of 2.0 percent in January, up from 1.6 percent the month before. Data from a third state, Bavaria showed a more tame 1.6 percent increase.
Traders said the figures indicate that preliminary west German CPI data which are likely to be released on Monday could show a gain of 1.7 percent -- higher than first forecast.

Stefan Schneider, economist at Banque Paribas in Frankfurt said the inflation rates, fuelled largely by higher oil and gas prices "took away the capital markets' feeling everything is hunky dory, with everyone thinking inflation is no problem."
Bunds had earlier been hurt by weak Treasuries and a surge in German import prices in December of 0.8 percent from the month before.
After a week that saw plenty of German data, including the Ifo report, M3 and today's inflation data, the focus will shift to the U.S. next week where the countdown to the FOMC meet starts.
The U.S. will release its fourth quarter employment cost index on Tuesday and gross domestic product figures on Friday.

Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum added to the negative rate picture, saying a quick tender operation conducted by the central bank this morning signalled steady interest rates in the near term.
Despite the bad inflation news, Bunds managed to boost the spread against T-notes to 95 basis points from 93 basis points, advancing further into post-unification record territory.
The yield curve was little changed with the spread between two- and 10-year notes steady at 233 basis points.
